_comment: Risk metadata the OT pilot declares for its own tools (REMORA_TOOL_METADATA_FILE).
Without it every pilot tool fell to the fail-closed default of critical/unknown,
and the state index in ot_bundle.py (coverage scope 'ot_plant') never applied,
because the policy engine saw domain 'unknown'. A monitoring read of a sensor
the plant inventory lists was therefore ungrounded and went to review along
with the valve moves (OT battery 2026-11-03: 0 of 5 monitoring reads completed).
This file is hashed into the policy bundle. Editing it moves the hash and
invalidates every outstanding lease. Declaring a tool lower than it is would
be the way to grant yourself something here, so each entry says why.

_why.read_sensor: Returns one sensor's current value and unit from the plant inventory and changes nothing. Low: the tool reads; where it reads is the target environment's concern, not the tier's. With REMORA_GROUNDED_READ_IN_PRODUCTION on, a read of a sensor the daily round names can complete without a person; every other clause of the grounded-read path still applies.
_why.adjust_setpoint: Moves a control loop's setpoint on the plant. Critical: a physical process change; every approval needs senior_authority and the cumulative movement limit applies.
_why.set_valve_position: Strokes a valve. Critical, as adjust_setpoint.
_why.acknowledge_alarm: Clears an alarm the operator must otherwise see. Critical: silencing an alarm is a safety-relevant state change even though it moves nothing.
_why.create_work_order: Creates a maintenance record that later authorises work. Critical: the record is itself an authority.
_why.close_work_order: Closes an authority record. Critical, as create_work_order.
_why._schema: schema_valid is true because the registry refuses an unknown sensor, loop, valve or alarm id before anything runs (ot_registry.py raises ValueError), and every write argument is a fixed shape.
